name: Acid Distortion Bass
description: A saw through the resonant 24 dB low-pass and the distortion, sliding between legato notes.

name: Acid Pulse Bass
description: A square through the resonant 24 dB low-pass, its envelope snapping shut, sliding between legato notes; accents open it further, and the ribbon turns the resonance up.

name: Chip Bass
description: A triangle an octave down, nothing more: the bass of a game console.

name: Click Bass
description: A saw an octave down with a burst of noise on each attack from the filter's quick envelope: a tight bass with a click.

name: Cross-Mod Bass
description: A triangle two octaves down, cross-modulated by a saw an octave above it, so its punch comes from the modulation rather than the filter; a short envelope on the cross-modulation depth makes each note bark.

name: Detuned Saw Bass
description: Two saws an octave down, one a few cents sharp, the filter snapping open on each note and closing to a warm body; harder notes snap brighter.

name: Distortion Bass
description: A saw an octave down through the Multi Effects' distortion, the filter snapping open: a dirty bass.

name: Dual Sub Bass
description: Dual: a plucked saw bass on the Upper part over a triangle sub two octaves down on the Lower.

name: Feedback Growl Bass
description: The feedback oscillator an octave down, its tone moved by a slow LFO so held notes growl and turn; a quick filter envelope for the attack, mono.

name: Fifth Bass
description: A saw an octave down with a saw a fifth above it: a heavy bass with a power chord in it.

name: Glide Sync Bass
description: A saw synced to a saw a little above it, sliding between legato notes, the filter's envelope giving each a bite.

name: Hard Saw Bass
description: Seven saws two octaves down, barely detuned, the filter opening with each note: a hard, full bass.

name: Hollow Pulse Bass
description: A wide pulse an octave down, the filter half open, no envelope: a hollow, steady bass.

name: Hoover Bass
description: Seven saws detuned wide two octaves down, dipping into pitch on each note: the rave hoover as a bass.

name: House Organ Bass
description: A square with another an octave up, short and dry: the organ bass of early house.

name: Legato Delay Bass
description: After the Sound-Creating Tips in the synth's owner's manual: a resonant saw two octaves down, its filter opened by the envelope, legato, doubled by a very short, full echo.

name: Neuro Bass
description: The feedback oscillator an octave down through the distortion, a quick filter envelope: snarling.

name: Octave Glide Bass
description: After the Sound-Creating Tips in the synth's owner's manual: two saws an octave apart two octaves down, a slow glide between legato notes, the bass lifted.

name: Plucked Pulse Bass
description: A narrow pulse an octave down, plucked short with no sustain: a bass for fast lines.

name: Psy Bass
description: A saw two octaves down, a very short filter and amp envelope: the tight sixteenth bass of psytrance.

name: Pulse Pluck Bass
description: A wide pulse an octave down with no sustain and a short resonant snap: a round plucked bass.

name: Pulse Width Bass
description: A pulse an octave down whose width drifts slowly, through the 24 dB low-pass and a quick envelope: round and moving.

name: Reese Bass
description: Seven saws two octaves down, slightly detuned so they beat slowly against each other, through a closed 24 dB low-pass: the drum and bass Reese.

name: Ribbon Bend Bass
description: A saw synced to a saw: the ribbon pushes the synced one up, from a round bass to a screaming one.

name: Ring Growl Bass
description: A saw an octave down with a triangle an octave above it ring-modulated in beside it: a growl on top of the bass.

name: Rolling Saw Octave Bass
description: After Airwave Music's video on remaking a classic trance bassline: a saw stack over a saw an octave down, no resonance, a quick envelope decay, mono.

name: Square Sub
description: A square two octaves down, the filter low enough to round it: the weight under a track.

name: Sub Triangle
description: A triangle two octaves down with the filter closed far enough to leave nearly a sine: the bass under a mix, not in front of it.

name: Sync Pluck Bass
description: A saw synced to a saw, its pitch envelope sweeping the synced one down fast, so each note starts with a vowel-like snap and falls into a round bass.

name: Synthwave Bass
description: A saw an octave down, short and bright, made for running eighth notes.

name: Triangle Mod Bass
description: Triangle modulation an octave down, its hollow, slightly metallic tone shaped by a short envelope.

name: Unison Saw Bass
description: A saw stacked in Unison an octave down, spread just wide enough to be thick, through a quick envelope.

name: Velocity Bass
description: A saw an octave down whose filter the velocity opens: soft notes round, hard ones snarl.

name: Wah Bass
description: A saw through a resonant band-pass that the envelope sweeps up and back on every note: a wah bass.

name: Wobble Reese
description: The Reese's detuned saws with the filter swung open and shut by a tempo-locked LFO in eighth triplets.

name: Cross-Mod Bell
description: A triangle cross-modulated by another at an inharmonic interval, struck and dying away like a bell; harder strikes ring brighter.

name: Crystal Bell
description: A triangle cross-modulated by a triangle two octaves above it, struck and ringing long, bright on top.

name: Glass Chime
description: Triangles two octaves apart, the upper a little louder, a slow swell into a long ring: glass struck softly.

name: Music Box
description: A triangle two octaves up, struck short with a long ring: a small music box.

name: Shimmer Bells
description: Triangles two octaves apart, struck softly into a long echo that keeps them shimmering.

name: Vibraphone
description: A triangle struck with a short click and a long ring, its level pulsing like a vibraphone's fan.

name: Brass Stab
description: Two saws an octave apart, the filter jumping open and falling back fast: a short brass hit for chords.

name: Pitch-Kissed Brass
description: After the Sound-Creating Tips in the synth's owner's manual: two saws, the second kissed sharp by a short pitch envelope, the filter and amp swelling like brass, a little cross-modulation and chorus.

name: Retro Brass
description: Two saws an octave apart, the filter rising after the attack and settling: the 80s synth brass.

name: Soft Horns
description: Two saws a few cents apart, the filter easing open over a slow attack: warm, distant horns.

name: Split Bass & Brass
description: Split at the B below middle C: a saw bass under the split, swelling saw brass above it.

name: Swell Brass
description: Two saws an octave apart whose filter swells open after the attack, the harder the note the brighter, a little chorus: a brass section's crescendo on every chord.

name: Alarm
description: A square whose pitch a square LFO flips between two notes: an alarm.

name: Bubbles
description: A resonant filter jumped to a new place every sixteenth by the sample-and-hold: bubbling water.

name: Dub Siren
description: A square swung up and down by a fast triangle LFO into a long, feeding-back echo: the sound system siren.

name: Falling Sweep
description: A saw starting high and sliding down slowly through the pitch envelope, a flanger on it: a long fall.

name: Feedback Wind
description: The feedback oscillator at its edge, its tone wandering on a slow random LFO through a resonant band-pass: wind through wires.

name: Laser Zap
description: A saw thrown high by the pitch envelope and dropping in an instant: the laser of an old arcade.

name: Noise Riser
description: White noise over a little saw through a resonant band-pass, its filter and level climbing slowly over the whole held note.

name: Random Bleeps
description: A plucked saw whose pitch the LFO's sample-and-hold jumps to a new place every sixteenth of the song: computer chatter.

name: Rising Laser
description: A saw starting low and shooting up through the pitch envelope's attack: a laser charging.

name: Siren
description: A square whose pitch a slow triangle LFO swings up and down a long way: a siren.

name: Space Drone
description: Synced saws swept very slowly by the LFO, under the jet phaser and a long echo: a drone in orbit.

name: Sync Sweep Drone
description: Two saws, the synced one swept up and down slowly by LFO 1 through the pitch: a drone that keeps changing color.

name: Wind
description: White noise through a resonant band-pass a slow random LFO moves: wind.

name: Digital Piano
description: Triangle modulation with a ring-modulated octave in it, struck and decaying: a bright digital piano.

name: Dual Organ & Brass
description: Dual: a square organ on the Upper part with saw brass swelling in under it on the Lower.

name: Feedback Organ
description: The feedback oscillator held back to a reedy tone, on and off at once, through the fast chorus.

name: House Piano Stab
description: Triangle modulation's bright tone struck short with a ring-modulated octave: the piano chord of a house track.

name: Mallet Keys
description: A triangle struck short with a click of the filter envelope: a wooden mallet.

name: Marimba
description: A triangle with a quiet octave above it, struck with a click and a short ring: a marimba.

name: Pulse Clav
description: A narrow pulse through a band-pass, plucked short, the strike opening the filter: funk keys.

name: Pulse Electric Piano
description: A wide pulse with a soft attack of the filter, decaying, panned slowly from side to side.

name: Pulse Harpsichord
description: A narrow pulse with another an octave up, plucked short and bright: a harpsichord's two choirs.

name: Ribbon Wah Keys
description: A pulse clav through a resonant band-pass that the ribbon sweeps like a wah pedal.

name: Ring Tine Keys
description: Two triangles two octaves apart, ring-modulated into a tine's bite at the strike and fading to a soft tone, with a tremolo the ribbon brings in.

name: Rotary Organ
description: A square and a saw an octave apart, on and off at once, through the twist effect turning like a speaker.

name: Saw Organ
description: A saw and a saw an octave up, on and off at once, through the fast chorus: a bright, buzzing organ.

name: Split Bass & Piano
description: Split at the B below middle C: a round pulse bass under the split, a bright digital piano above it.

name: Square Organ
description: A square and a square an octave up, sounding at once and stopping at once, through the fast chorus: a compact combo organ.

name: Supersaw Keys
description: Seven saws struck and decaying to a low sustain: keys for big chords.

name: Sync Organ
description: A saw synced to a saw an octave and a half above, on and off at once: a bright, vocal organ.

name: Tremolo Keys
description: Two triangles two octaves apart, ring-modulated for a tine's bite, panning side to side under the auto pan.

name: Triangle Mod Keys
description: Triangle modulation's thin, bright tone under a quick filter envelope, sustaining a little: keys between a toy piano and a vibraphone.

name: Velocity Layer Keys
description: Triangles two octaves apart, ring-modulated: soft notes are mellow tines, hard ones bark brightly, and louder.

name: Anthem Superstring
description: After AtomicA Sounds' video on the synth's history and the classic trance sound: the seven saws alone at full mix, the bass and treble lifted, chorus on, quick to speak and to stop; a short panning echo widens it, standing in for the video's long reverb.

name: Breath Flute
description: A soft triangle with a breath of noise, the attack easing in, a vibrato that waits before it starts, a short room of echo.

name: Chip Lead
description: A narrow pulse with nothing filtered away and a quick vibrato that waits a moment: an 8-bit lead.

name: Clarinet
description: A square through a low-pass that follows the keys, the attack easing in, a delayed vibrato: a clarinet.

name: Detuned Square Lead
description: Two squares a few cents apart, beating gently, through an open 24 dB low-pass: a fat, round lead.

name: Distortion Lead
description: Two saws a few cents apart through the Multi Effects' distortion, mono with a quick glide: a lead that growls when played hard.

name: Dual Detuned Stack
description: Dual: the same two-saw lead on both parts, Part Detune pulling them apart and the panning echo spreading them: one lead as wide as two.

name: Dual Layer Saw Lead
description: After Dash Glitch's second video on a free emulation of the synth: both parts as tight saw stacks at full mix, one an octave up and quieter, a plucked filter envelope that opens with velocity, treble up, chorus on both and a dotted echo.

name: Dual Octave Lead
description: Dual: a saw lead on the Upper part over a square an octave down on the Lower, both gliding.

name: Dual Sub Lead
description: Dual: a square lead on the Upper part over a triangle two octaves down on the Lower, both mono.

name: Euro Octave Lead
description: Seven saws with a saw an octave above them, bright and wide, plucked open by the filter: the 90s dance lead.

name: Feedback Howl
description: The feedback oscillator alone, mono and gliding, a vibrato that fades in on long notes and a dotted echo. The ribbon drives the feedback harder and opens the filter.

name: Fifth Lead
description: A saw with another a fifth above it, mono: every note a power chord.

name: Gated Trance Lead
description: Seven saws chopped in sixteenths by a square LFO on the amplifier, locked to the song: a gated lead.

name: Glide Triangle Lead
description: A triangle two octaves of glide wide, mono and legato: a pure, singing line with nothing but its slide.

name: Goa Glide Saws
description: After Dash Glitch's video on a free emulation of the synth: a lightly detuned saw stack with a saw an octave up, mono and gliding, through a resonant high-pass a slow LFO moves, and the slow chorus.

name: Hard Lead
description: Seven saws through the distortion with a pitch envelope kicking each note: a hardstyle lead.

name: High-Pass Saw Lead
description: A saw through the resonant high-pass, so it cuts through a mix without filling it, a quick glide.

name: Jet Phase Lead
description: Seven saws through the jet phaser, its sweep riding every held note.

name: Lever Vibrato Lead
description: Two saws a few cents apart, mono with a quick glide; the modulation lever brings in LFO 2's vibrato, and the filter opens with the strike.

name: Metal Cross Lead
description: A triangle cross-modulated by a pulse an octave above, bright and clangy, harder the harder it is played; the ribbon brings the modulation from glassy to snarling.

name: Neon Lead
description: A square with a saw a few cents off, chorus and a long echo: a lead from a night drive.

name: Oboe
description: A narrow pulse through a band-pass, a quick attack and a delayed vibrato: a reedy oboe.

name: Ocarina
description: The feedback oscillator held back to a soft, hollow tone, an easy attack and a slow vibrato that comes in on held notes.

name: Octave Square Lead
description: A square with a narrower pulse an octave above it, gliding mono, a touch of delayed vibrato: an old computer game's lead, grown up.

name: Pitch-Swoop Saw Lead
description: After Dash Glitch's second video on a free emulation of the synth: a wide saw stack an octave down, each note thrown sharp by the pitch envelope and swooping back into pitch, chorus and a dotted echo spreading it.

name: Pulse Width Solo
description: A pulse whose width the first LFO sweeps, a saw a few cents above it, the 24 dB low-pass opening on each note and settling. A gentle glide; the ribbon brings in vibrato.

name: Rave Hoover
description: Seven saws detuned wide, stacked in Unison, dipping into pitch on each note through a slow glide and a slow flanger. The early-90s rave stab and lead in one.

name: Remix Main Lead
description: After NiamorH's notes on remaking a trance remix on the synth: one saw stack through the 24 dB low-pass, its envelope snapping open and falling back fast, a little resonance, chorus and a short eighth-note echo.

name: Ribbon Sweep Lead
description: Two saws behind a resonant 24 dB low-pass held half shut: the ribbon opens it all the way and turns the resonance up as it goes.

name: Ring Octave Lead
description: A saw ring-modulated by a triangle an octave above it, hard and hollow at once, mono; the ribbon mixes the dry saw back in.

name: Stream Seven-Saw Lead
description: After a Vulture Culture livestream on the synth: the seven saws at a middling detune with the mix high, a long sustain and release, chorus and a long dotted-eighth echo panning across.

name: Sync Scream
description: Two saws, the second synced to the first and thrown an octave and a half up by the pitch envelope, so every note opens with a tearing sweep. Mono; the ribbon pushes the sweep further.

name: Talking Lead
description: A saw through a resonant band-pass that a tempo-locked LFO swings in quarter notes: a lead that talks in time.

name: Trance Pluck Lead
description: Seven saws whose filter snaps open and falls to a middling sustain, so a fast line plucks and a held note sings, under a long dotted echo.

name: Triangle Mod Lead
description: Triangle modulation's bright tone as a mono lead, a slow vibrato coming in and a dotted echo.

name: Twist Lead
description: A pulse whose width the LFO moves, through the Multi Effects' twist: a lead that seems to turn in place.

name: Unison Feedback Lead
description: The feedback oscillator stacked in Unison, mono with a glide: one huge, rough voice.

name: Unison Pulse Lead
description: A pulse whose width the LFO sweeps, stacked in Unison and spread wide: one note as thick as a section.

name: Whistle
description: A triangle two octaves up with a quick vibrato and a little glide: someone whistling.

name: Auto-Pan Shimmer
description: Two pulses an octave apart, slowly swelling, swept from side to side by the auto pan under a long echo.

name: Breathing Band Pad
description: Filtered noise ringing near a pitch, beside a soft saw, through the band-pass a slow LFO moves up and down: a pad that breathes.

name: Cold Pad
description: A narrow pulse through the high-pass, its width drifting, slowly in: thin and cold.

name: Cross-Mod Pad
description: A triangle gently cross-modulated by a triangle an octave above it, swelling in: a pad with a metallic edge that the ribbon sharpens.

name: Dark Drone Pad
description: Seven saws an octave down through a nearly closed 24 dB low-pass with a little resonance: a dark bed.

name: Deep House Pad
description: A wide pulse with a saw a few cents off through a soft low-pass, a slow bow and a little echo.

name: Distant Choir
description: Seven saws through a band-pass a slow LFO moves between vowels, far back behind a long echo.

name: Dual Bell & Strings
description: Dual: a struck triangle bell on the Upper part over pulse-width strings bowed in on the Lower.

name: Dual Glass Ambience
description: Dual: ringing noise tones on the Upper part over slow triangle pads on the Lower, both into long echoes.

name: Dual Octave Saws
description: Dual: seven saws on the Upper part and seven an octave down on the Lower, slightly detuned between them.

name: Dual Pluck & Pad
description: Dual: a plucked saw on the Upper part over a slow pad on the Lower: every chord struck and then held.

name: Dual Strings & Choir
description: Dual: pulse-width strings on the Upper part over a band-pass saw choir on the Lower, both bowed in slowly.

name: Feedback Pad
description: The feedback oscillator swelling in, its tone drifting on a slow LFO, under the slow phaser.

name: Flange Pad
description: Two saws through the deep flanger, its sweep turning a held chord into a slow jet.

name: Glacier Pad
description: The noise ringing as a pure tone under triangles two octaves apart, very slow in and out, a long echo.

name: High-Pass Sweep Pad
description: After the Sound-Creating Tips in the synth's owner's manual: the seven saws through the high-pass, shut and opening as its slow envelope falls, a long echo at full and the chorus just short of it.

name: Jet Phase Pad
description: Seven saws through the jet phaser, swelling in: the sound of a jet passing overhead in slow motion.

name: Layered Saw & Sine Pad
description: Dual: seven saws swelling in on the Upper part over a soft triangle an octave down on the Lower, the two slightly apart in time.

name: Liquid Pad
description: A triangle with a quiet saw an octave up under a slow filter LFO and a long echo: the soft bed of liquid drum and bass.

name: Night Drive Pad
description: A pulse whose width sweeps slowly, through the slow flanger, swelling in: the pad under a neon skyline.

name: Noise Sine Choir
description: The filtered noise ringing as a pure tone over soft seven saws, slowly in and out: an airy choir.

name: Noise Sweep Pad
description: White noise under two saws through a band-pass a slow LFO sweeps: air moving through a pad.

name: Phase Drift Pad
description: A wide pulse and a triangle under the slow phaser, the pulse's width drifting on its own LFO, the filter closing slowly while a chord is held.

name: Pulse Sweep Pad
description: A pulse whose width sweeps slowly under a filter that the LFO opens on another slow cycle.

name: Ribbon Morph Pad
description: Seven saws with a triangle an octave above: the ribbon crossfades between them, opens the filter and slows the chorus's swirl into a flange.

name: Ring Glass Pad
description: Two triangles an octave apart, ring-modulated into a glassy shimmer on the note's third harmonic, swelling slowly through a clear chorus and a long echo; the ribbon opens the filter.

name: Slow Bloom
description: Seven saws whose filter opens over many seconds while a chord is held: a sound that blooms.

name: Slow Wah Pad
description: A saw and a pulse through a resonant 24 dB low-pass that a slow LFO opens and closes over several bars.

name: Split Pad & Bell
description: Split at middle C: a warm saw pad under the split, struck triangle bells above it.

name: Supersaw Atmosphere
description: Seven saws wide apart through the high-pass, rising slowly out of nothing into a long echo.

name: Tempo Gate Pad
description: A seven-saw pad chopped in eighth notes by a square LFO on the amplifier, locked to the song's tempo.

name: Tremolo Pad
description: Two saws whose level a slow LFO pulses, swelling in: a pad that breathes in long waves.

name: Triangle Mod Pad
description: Triangle modulation's bright, glassy tone, swelling slowly, a slow LFO moving the modulation.

name: Twist Pad
description: Two saws through the Multi Effects' twist, slowly in and out: a pad that never sits still.

name: Underwater
description: Two saws far under a closed low-pass with a slow LFO moving it, the pitch drifting a little: underwater.

name: Unison Triangle Pad
description: A triangle stacked in Unison and spread, swelling in slowly: soft, wide and hollow.

name: Uplifting Supersaw Pad
description: Seven saws at full mix with a saw an octave above, swelling in under the slow chorus and a long echo: the breakdown chord.

name: Velvet Pad
description: A triangle and a saw an octave up, the saw quiet, through a soft low-pass, slowly in and slowly out.

name: Vowel Saw Choir
description: Seven saws, lightly detuned, through a resonant band-pass so they sing like an open vowel; the ribbon moves the vowel.

name: Warm Analog Pad
description: Two saws a few cents apart through a soft 24 dB low-pass, swelling and fading slowly: the plain warm pad.

name: Chip Noise Snare
description: White noise through the high-pass, cut short: an 8-bit snare.

name: Noise Hat
description: White noise through the high-pass, cut off almost at once: a closed hi-hat.

name: Noise Snare
description: A triangle body thrown down by the pitch envelope under a burst of white noise through the band-pass.

name: Pitch Drop Kick
description: A triangle two octaves down, thrown high by the pitch envelope and dropping fast into a short thump.

name: Pitch Tom
description: A triangle an octave down whose pitch falls through a short envelope: a tom that follows the keys.

name: Pulse Rim
description: A narrow pulse two octaves up, struck and gone: a rimshot's click.

name: Shaker
description: White noise through the high-pass, a short swell and a short fall: a shaker.

name: Zap Kick
description: A square two octaves down, its pitch falling from very high in an instant: an electro kick's zap.

name: Band-Pass Pluck
description: Two saws through a resonant band-pass, plucked short: nasal and bright.

name: Big Room Stab
description: Seven saws wide apart with a saw an octave below, cut short: the festival stab.

name: Distortion Pluck
description: A saw plucked short through the Multi Effects' distortion and an eighth-note echo.

name: Dub Chord
description: Two saws through a soft band-pass, cut short into a long, darkening echo: the dub techno chord.

name: Harp Pluck
description: A triangle and a saw an octave up, the saw quiet, plucked with a medium ring: a soft harp.

name: High-Pass Pluck
description: Seven saws through the high-pass, plucked short with a quick filter envelope and a dotted echo: thin and bright, made to sit above a mix.

name: Koto Pluck
description: A narrow pulse struck with a small upward bend that settles at once: a plucked string from the East.

name: Melody Ring Pluck
description: After a trance melody sheet for the synth shared by ariki1 on Vintage Synth Explorer: a saw stack ring-modulated with a synced pulse, plucked by both envelopes, the treble up, chorus and a short echo.

name: Minimal Blip
description: A triangle struck very short: a blip for minimal techno.

name: Noise Sine Pluck
description: The filtered noise turned up until it rings as a pure tone, plucked short, with a short panning echo.

name: Ring Pluck
description: A saw ring-modulated by a triangle an octave above it, plucked short: bright and metallic.

name: Sitar Pluck
description: A narrow pulse struck with a small bend down into the note and a buzzing band-pass: a sitar.

name: Split Sub & Pluck
description: Split at middle C: a triangle sub under the split, a seven-saw pluck into a dotted echo above it.

name: Square Echo Pluck
description: A square plucked short into an eighth-note echo that keeps going: a sequence from one note.

name: Steel Drum
description: A triangle cross-modulated by another an octave above it, struck short: a steel pan.

name: Supersaw Pluck
description: Seven saws cut short by both envelopes, a little resonance on the filter's snap and a dotted echo.

name: Sync Stab
description: Synced saws, the synced one a fifth up, cut short by both envelopes: a bright chord stab.

name: Techno Stab
description: A saw and a pulse through a resonant low-pass snapping shut: the stab of a warehouse record.

name: Accent Pulse Sequence
description: The arpeggiator on its accented sixteenth pattern, up and down, over a short pulse whose filter the accents open; an eighth-note echo.

name: Arcade Arp
description: The arpeggiator up three octaves in sixteenths on a narrow pulse: an arcade machine's fanfare.

name: Chip Arp
description: The arpeggiator in thirty-seconds over one octave on a square: a chord the way a game console played one.

name: Falling Arp
description: The arpeggiator walking down two octaves in eighths, a bell-like triangle pair cross-modulated a little.

name: Organ Arp
description: The arpeggiator up and down two octaves in eighths on the square organ.

name: Random Arp Pluck
description: The arpeggiator picking the held notes at random in sixteenths over two octaves, a short saw pluck.

name: Sixteenth Saw Arp
description: The arpeggiator up two octaves in sixteenths at the song's tempo, over plucked seven saws and a dotted echo. Hold a chord.

name: Split Acid & Stab
description: Split at middle C: an acid bass sliding under the split, a resonant stab above it.

name: Split Arp & Pad
description: Split at middle C: the arpeggiator runs the keys below it up and down in sixteenths on a plucked pulse, while the keys above play a soft pad.

name: Split Bass Arp
description: Split at middle C: the arpeggiator runs the keys below it in sixteenths as a plucked bass, while the keys above play a saw lead.

name: Thirty-Second Arp
description: The arpeggiator in thirty-second notes over three octaves of a plucked pulse: a fast shimmer from a held chord.

name: Triplet Arp
description: The arpeggiator up and down in sixteenth triplets, a seven-saw pluck rolling over the beat.

name: Chamber Strings
description: Two saws a few cents apart through a soft low-pass, a medium bow and the slow chorus: a small section.

name: High-Pass Strings
description: Seven saws through the high-pass, bowed in: the strings' airy top without their body.

name: Octave Ensemble
description: Seven saws with a saw an octave below them, bowed in slowly through the slow chorus: a full ensemble.

name: Pulse Width Strings
description: A pulse whose width a slow LFO sweeps, with a saw a few cents off, bowed in and out slowly through the slow chorus: the string machine sound.

name: Seven-Saw Strings
description: After the Sound-Creating Tips in the synth's owner's manual: the seven saws at full mix, bowed in slowly, the echo at full and the chorus just short of it, so it keeps its body in mono.

name: Split Bass & Strings
description: Split at the B below middle C: a mono saw bass under the split, slow pulse-width strings above it.

name: Synth Pizzicato
description: Two saws plucked short with a fast filter decay: strings played with the fingers.

name: Native Neutral
description: Ten-voice Native engine with a neutral supported patch for real-time playback and automation.
